review_agent_is_blocked_on_us: Most of its commits say 'audit paused, queue full' -- it stops auditing while open/ is large, so throughput is limited by the fix agent. Turnaround on a handoff is usually minutes; four are queued for it now.
operational_rules_learned_the_hard_way: backend `npm run lint` is `eslint --fix` and rewrites source. Gate on `npx eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` instead.
Run backend unit tests as `TZ=UTC npm run test:unit`; some specs count periods against fixtures and flip under other offsets.
Jest here is v30: the flag is `--testPathPatterns` (plural).
Frontend `npm run test` takes ~9 minutes (628 files). Iterate with `npx vitest run <path>`; run the full suite once before pushing.

A FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED in this sandbox, and so are chained short sleeps. To wait for a long job: start it with run_in_background, then a second background job `until [ "$(ps aux | grep -c '[v]itest')" -eq 0 ]; do sleep 15; done`, or the Monitor tool with the same until-loop.

NEVER git stash to check a test fails without the fix WHILE a full-suite run is in flight -- the running suite reads the reverted file mid-run and its result is worthless. Order: per-file revert checks FIRST, then start the full suite, then leave the tree alone until it reports.

A stop hook nags about uncommitted changes every turn, and the suite takes ~9 minutes, so it WILL fire while you wait. Do not let it push you into committing on partial evidence. Bound the risk cheaply instead and say so in the commit message: run the touched suites, run the consumers' suites, check `grep -rn 'toMatchSnapshot' --include=*.test.tsx src | wc -l` (0 today, so an added DOM attribute cannot break a snapshot), confirm project-wide tsc. That was enough for REV-017 and REV-018. WAIT for the full suite when the change is a shared component with many call sites (REV-012, 32 sites) or touches a submit path where the documented precedent is silent DATA LOSS (REV-009/010, issue #806).
The coordination worktree is refreshed with `git reset --hard`, which does NOT delete untracked files -- a newly written DEC survives it.
Pipe a script's output to `head` and you can get a BrokenPipeError traceback AFTER the work already succeeded. Check the effect before believing the traceback.
NEVER write a SHA you have not read from git. Use `git rev-parse <short>`; a full SHA typed from memory is fabricated and lands in the coordination record. Done once this session and corrected.

CHECK A LABEL STRING AGAINST THE CATALOG BEFORE ASSERTING ON IT. `queryByText('Payment Amount')` passes forever against a label that is really 'Payment Amount (required)' -- a negative assertion on a string that does not exist is vacuous by construction. Read the en catalog (`python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('src/i18n/messages/en/accounts.json'))['loanFields'])"`) rather than guessing.

A MOCK THAT DISCARDS AN ARGUMENT CANNOT TEST THAT ARGUMENT. REV-015/031 were invisible because the useNumberFormat mocks were `(amount) => ...`, dropping currencyCode. Same class as a `{ data: [...] }` mock with no `pagination`. Mirror the real fallback (`code || default`).

A CHART TEST'S RECHARTS MOCK IS OFTEN `YAxis: () => null, Tooltip: () => null`, so the tick formatter and tooltip content never run. Render their output, and have YAxis pass a tick INDEX second: recharts calls tickFormatter as (value, index), so `tickFormatter={formatCurrencyAxis}` by reference silently receives 0 as its currency and the `string | number` parameter absorbs it. Always wrap.

FIREEVENT.CLICK ON A DISABLED BUTTON IS A NO-OP, so a 'double click is ignored' test written that way passes regardless. Invoke the hook directly (write it to a sink object inside `useEffect` -- eslint bans reassigning an outer variable during render).

A TEST CAN BE NON-VACUOUS YET STILL NOT FAIL AGAINST THE ORIGINAL CODE. REV-018's re-entry test: the original prevented double-apply BY ACCIDENT (it nulled the preview before awaiting, so the second call early-returned) -- a side effect of the bug itself. When a revert run does not fail, work out WHY before either deleting the test or claiming it as regression coverage, and write the reason down.

PREFER A REQUIRED PROP when threading a per-entity identity (a currency, an editing mode): tsc then enumerates every unfixed call site -- it found five for PayoffComparisonChart and three for LoanFields. Prefer OPTIONAL with a default for a capability a shared component's other callers do not need (ConfirmDialog's isBusy, so its other 29 sites are untouched).

'AN EXISTING TEST ALREADY COVERS THIS' IS A CLAIM ABOUT WHICH BRANCH THE TEST RUNS. DateInput.test.tsx's four 'touch mode' tests all sit under a describe whose beforeEach sets DD/MM/YYYY, so they exercise touch-FORMATTED mode and say nothing about touch-browser. I nearly disputed half of REV-012 on that basis.

DateInput has FOUR modes (touch/desktop x browser/formatted) from `getInputMode(dateFormat)`, dateFormat being a USER PREFERENCE. touch-browser has no `if (mode === ...)` branch -- it is the fallback `return` at the end. Check all four when changing a handler contract.

AN EXISTING TEST ASSERTING THE BEHAVIOUR A FINDING CALLS A BUG IS A FORK. Decide it by asking whether a CLAUDE.md rule or in-repo pattern says which artifact is right. Yes -> replace the test and say so in the commit (REV-039's 'handles loadTransactions error gracefully'; REV-009's 'does not show loan fields when editing existing LOAN account', whose comment merely restated the condition while a MORTGAGE already did the opposite). No -> escalate (REV-017's historical-rate test, whose comment showed deliberate intent; DEC-20260803-006).

CHECK THE BACKEND DTO BEFORE ASSUMING A FRONTEND FIX NEEDS AN API CHANGE. REV-010 looked like it needed a schema change; UpdateAccountDto already accepted `string | null` with `@ValidateIf(... !== null)` for all four fields, so the fix was frontend-only and the finding's recommended 'allow null in the form schema' was unnecessary (the cleanup runs post-validation anyway).
transactions.status is NULLABLE (schema.sql:274). Never `status != 'VOID'` / `Not(TransactionStatus.VOID)`; use the entity's isVoid getter in JS or `(t.status IS NULL OR t.status != 'VOID')` in SQL.
Reuse an existing translated key across namespaces where the copy is identical. A new en-only key costs ~36 parity failures.
